skill.name: pymc-bayesian-modeling
skill.description: Bayesian modeling support for PyMC, including model design, prior selection, MCMC diagnostics, posterior checks, and LOO/WAIC comparison.
skill.summary: Build, diagnose, and compare Bayesian models with PyMC and ArviZ.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, Bayesian terms, and dictionary key access in model comparison code. No evidence of prompt injection, network access, shell execution, or credential handling was found. One medium semantic issue remains because the workflow demonstrates pickle deserialization without a trust warning.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer NetCDF for InferenceData artifacts. If pickle guidance remains, warn users to load only trusted self-created files and avoid shared or downloaded pickle files.

static_findings.snippet: - Use named dimensions with `coords` for clarity
- Use named dimensions (`dims`) instead of `shape` when possible
- Use `pm.Data()` for values that will be updated for predictions
- `pm.StudentT('theta', nu=3, mu=0, sigma=1)` - Robust to outliers
- `pm.LKJCorr('corr', n=n_vars, eta=2)` - eta=1 uniform, eta>1 prefers identity
- `pm.Normal('y', mu=mu, sigma=sigma)` - Default for continuous data
- `pm.StudentT('y', nu=nu, mu=mu, sigma=sigma)` - Robust to outliers
- Discrete parameters → Use `pm.Metropolis()` for discrete vars

- **`model_diagnostics.py`**: Automated diagnostic checking and report generation. Functions: `check

content.value_statement: Bayesian modeling requires careful priors, diagnostics, and model checks. This skill guides PyMC workflows from model setup through posterior validation and comparison.
actual_capabilities: Guides linear, logistic, hierarchical, count, and time series model patterns in PyMC.
Explains prior selection for scale, unbounded, positive, probability, and likelihood parameters.
Provides sampling guidance for NUTS, Metropolis, SMC, ADVI, and related convergence issues.
Includes diagnostic helpers for R-hat, ESS, divergences, trace plots, rank plots, and summary exports.
Includes model comparison utilities for LOO, WAIC, Pareto-k checks, and model averaging.
Provides reusable templates for linear regression and hierarchical model workflows.
limitations: It does not install PyMC, ArviZ, NumPy, pandas, matplotlib, or other runtime dependencies.
It cannot guarantee model convergence or statistical validity for every dataset.
The helper scripts require valid ArviZ InferenceData objects from completed model fits.
Pickle examples should only be used with trusted local files.

use_cases.title: Design a Bayesian Regression Model
use_cases.description: Build a PyMC regression model with appropriate priors, standardized predictors, sampling settings, and posterior checks.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Sampling Problems
use_cases.description: Review R-hat, ESS, divergences, tree depth, and trace plots to decide how to improve a model.

use_cases.title: Compare Candidate Models
use_cases.description: Use LOO, WAIC, Pareto-k diagnostics, and model averaging to compare Bayesian models responsibly.

prompt_templates.title: Start a PyMC Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a PyMC model for this dataset. Identify the outcome, predictors, likely likelihood, useful priors, and required data preparation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Priors
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these model variables and suggest weakly informative priors. Explain why each prior is suitable and what prior predictive checks I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Sampling Diagnostics
prompt_templates.prompt: Interpret these PyMC diagnostics and propose changes. Focus on divergences, R-hat, ESS, tree depth, parameterization, and target_accept settings.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Bayesian Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these candidate PyMC models using LOO or WAIC. Explain Pareto-k reliability, uncertainty in differences, and whether model averaging is appropriate.

output_examples.input: A user has grouped observations and wants partial pooling by group.
output: Recommended a hierarchical model with group-level intercepts and non-centered parameterization.
Defined prior predictive checks before sampling.
Listed diagnostics to verify before interpreting group effects.

output_examples.input: A user has several fitted models and wants to choose one.
output: Suggested LOO comparison with log likelihood enabled.
Explained how to inspect Pareto-k warnings.
Recommended model averaging when differences are small relative to uncertainty.

output_examples.input: A user sees divergences and low effective sample size after sampling.
output: Recommended higher target_accept, stronger priors, and reparameterization.
Suggested rerunning diagnostics before reporting results.

best_practices: Run prior predictive checks before fitting the model.
Check R-hat, ESS, divergences, and posterior predictive fit before interpretation.
Use named dimensions, fixed random seeds, and documented priors for reproducible workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not interpret posterior summaries before checking sampling diagnostics.
Do not use flat priors when weakly informative priors are available.
Do not compare models with LOO or WAIC unless log likelihood values are available and reliable.

faq.question: Does this skill run PyMC models for me?
faq.answer: It provides guidance, templates, and helper scripts. The user still needs a Python environment with the required packages.

faq.question: Which PyMC version does it target?
faq.answer: The guidance targets the modern PyMC 5.x API and ArviZ based diagnostics.

faq.question: Can it help with hierarchical models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes non-centered hierarchical model guidance and a reusable hierarchical template.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple Bayesian models?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains LOO, WAIC, Pareto-k reliability checks, and model averaging.

faq.question: Does it replace statistical review?
faq.answer: No. It supports workflow design and diagnostics, but users should still validate assumptions and domain fit.

faq.question: Is saving models with pickle safe?
faq.answer: Only for trusted local files. Users should not load pickle files from untrusted sources.
